Prime location, in the heart of Valencia’s historic center Valencia, one of Spain’s largest and most important cities, combines history, culture, and dynamism in every corner. Located on the shores of the Mediterranean Sea, it attracts tourists from all over the world, especially during the summer months. The city hosts major international trade fairs, solidifying its position as an emerging destination brimming with opportunities. Strolling through its streets reveals the capital’s rich cultural and culinary heritage, where time flies by amidst monuments, squares, and markets. And when it’s time to refuel, nothing beats savoring authentic Valencian Paella, right in its place of origin. situación y actividades Activities in Valencia What to see and Do in Valencia Plaza de la Virgen In the historic heart of Valencia, this square, which originated as the ancient Roman forum, hosts important events such as the Offering to the Virgin of the Forsaken during the Fallas festival. Surrounding it are the Cathedral, the Basilica of Our Lady of the Forsaken, and the Turia Fountain, all must-see attractions. 400 meters from MORELLANA El Almudín Built on the site of the former Muslim fortress in the early 14th century, this historic building served as a center for the storage and sale of wheat. Its murals, featuring popular paintings of guilds and patron saints, now adorn temporary exhibitions showcasing the city’s rich cultural heritage. 500 meters from MORELLANA Lonja de la Seda La Lonja de la Seda, joya de la arquitectura gótica civil, comenzó a construirse en 1483. Emblemática en Valencia, refleja el auge medieval del comercio de la seda y su importancia como centro de mercaderes. 140 meters from MORELLANA Baños Árabes del Almirante Este edificio mudéjar, junto al Palacio de los Almirantes de Aragón, fue construido en el siglo XIV como un auténtico hammam islámico. Recuperado en 1986, permite apreciar su función y diseño originales tras siglos de transformaciones. 500 meters from MORELLANA Mercado Central Ubicado en la plaza del Mercado, junto a la Lonja de la Seda y la plaza de la Ciudad de Brujas, este emblemático edificio destaca por su estructura con columnas de hierro, y alberga el mayor mercado de productos frescos de Europa. 100 meters from MORELLANA Ciudad de las Artes y las Ciencias The City of Arts and Sciences is an impressive 350,000 m² scientific and cultural complex located on the banks of the Turia River. Opened in 1996, it comprises six distinct areas and is conceived as a city within a city, a prime example of modern architecture. 2.8 km from MORELLANA Iglesia de San Nicolás Begun in the 13th century as one of the “First Christian Parishes,” this church combines a 15th-century Gothic structure with 17th-century Baroque decoration. Restored in 2016, it is considered by specialists to be comparable to the Sistine Chapel in the Vatican. 350 meters from MORELLANA Mercado de Colón Located in the First Ensanche district, this modernist building stands in the heart of Valencia’s commercial district. It is one of the city’s most iconic landmarks, with details that evoke Gaudí’s unique style in Barcelona. 1.2 km from MORELLANA Torres del Quart The Quart Towers, one of the twelve gates of Valencia’s old city wall, are a prominent historical monument. Built in the 15th century, they served as access and defense for travelers coming from Castile. 700 meters from MORELLANA Torres de Serranos The Serranos Towers, part of the old Christian wall of Valencia and an example of 14th-century Valencian Gothic architecture, have served as a triumphal arch, prison and stage for the Fallera Mayor’s proclamation during the Fallas festival. 600 meters from MORELLANA Plaza Redonda In the heart of the city’s historic center, this neoclassical square is surrounded by thirty-four buildings of varying styles and sizes. Its charming plaza reflects the city’s traditions and its historical commercial function, inviting visitors to stroll and discover its unique atmosphere. 150 meters from MORELLANA Iglesia y Torre de Santa Catalina The Church of Santa Catalina, one of the oldest in the city, was built on the site of a former mosque after the Reconquista. With Gothic and Baroque details, its iconic tower marks the entrance to the lively and emblematic Mercat district. 140 meters from MORELLANA Paseo Marítimo de la Malvarrosa Valencia’s seafront promenade runs along the beaches of Las Arenas and La Malvarrosa, connecting the city to the sea. With its bike path, restaurants, and marine sculptures, it invites you to enjoy the atmosphere, the cuisine, and the Mediterranean breeze. A 5.5 km de MORELLANA Las Fallas de Valencia The Fallas of Valencia, celebrated every March, are one of Spain’s most iconic festivals. The city is filled with cardboard and wooden monuments, music, color, and tradition, culminating in the spectacular Cremà, the burning of the figures amidst emotion and fire. Semana Santa Marinera The Maritime Holy Week in Valencia is celebrated in the seaside neighborhoods with processions full of tradition, faith, and color. Brotherhoods, floats, and music fill the streets along the sea, creating a unique atmosphere that blends devotion, culture, and local heritage.
